question: Can a small history-conditioned continuous mixture router actually learn from factual prediction error without context labels, and is the gain more than a conventional similarly sized trained network or handcoded prior?
null: Learned routing does not reduce disjoint DEV validation error versus initialization/history ablations or a near-param-matched fully trained conventional MLP.

design.phase: prototype mechanism only, not native fast-memory runtime integration
design.target: factual observed continuous sensor difference, MSE
design.router: trainable continuous 16->24->16->1 two-expert sigmoid gate, learned from factual prediction error alone
design.baseline: trainable conventional MLP direct 17->24->16->1, trained on same examples/updates with near-equal parameters
design.full_batch_access: only to training examples; validation for reporting not model selection
ablations: P6-style hardcoded latest opposite action-pair signed effect
design.loss_windows: record at updates 100,200,300,400,500,600, require ≤1% last-five spread only as diagnostic: do not retune or relabel
design.initial_exploration_disclosure: Model architecture and learning-rate trialed in isolated development before freeze. This is not preregistered independent scientific evaluation.
prospective_performance_diagnostics: trained router final validation MSE <0.8*untrained same network
trained router lower validation MSE than P6-style handcoded prior
trained router lower validation MSE than trained conventional MLP
trained router lower validation MSE than shuffled history
trained router lower validation MSE than no history
design.engineering_pass: exact-source full Windows/WSL regression, actual gradient changes, matched examples/updates, <5% parameter difference, valid causal history/negative controls; NO pass requirement on outcome superiority

science.future_study: fully trained matched FLOPs/actions/compute controls, independently born sealed worlds, action-consequence transfer/interference/cold retention, separate first-use owner authorization
